\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಅಳುಕು} (aḷuku)}{ಅಳುಕು (aḷuku)}]{\kn{ಅಳುಕು} (aḷuku) — to waver; to flinch}

\label{lesson:KA-C420-aluku}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a crisis, then the Kannada for unavoidable.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಅಳುಕು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಅಳುಕು}} — \emph{aḷuku} — \textquotedblleft{}to waver; to flinch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಕತ್ತಲೆಯ} \kn{ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಹೋಗಲು} \kn{ನಾನು} \kn{ಅಳುಕಿದೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kattaleya dāriyalli hōgalu nānu aḷukide.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I flinched at going down the dark road.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \kn{ಅಳುಕಿದೆ}, \emph{aḷukide}.

Often negative: \kn{ಅಳುಕದೆ}, without flinching.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಅಳುಕು}} (\emph{aḷuku}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 306 lists Kannada \emph{aḷuku}, \textquotedblleft{}to fear\textquotedblright{}, beside Tamil \emph{aḷukku}, \textquotedblleft{}to be frightened\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aḷuku}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aḷuku}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kattaleya dāriyalli hōgalu nānu aḷukide.} — I flinched at going down the dark road.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a crisis, then the Kannada for unavoidable, then say \emph{aḷuku} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಅಳುಕು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To waver; to flinch\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಎಚ್ಚೆತ್ತುಕೊ} (eccettuko)}{ಎಚ್ಚೆತ್ತುಕೊ (eccettuko)}]{\kn{ಎಚ್ಚೆತ್ತುಕೊ} (eccettuko) — to wake up to}

\label{lesson:KA-C420-eccettuko}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for unavoidable, then the Kannada for to waver.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಎಚ್ಚೆತ್ತುಕೊ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಎಚ್ಚೆತ್ತುಕೊ}} — \emph{eccettuko} — \textquotedblleft{}to wake up to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಅಪಾಯದ} \kn{ಸುದ್ದಿ} \kn{ಕೇಳಿ} \kn{ಜನರು} \kn{ಎಚ್ಚೆತ್ತುಕೊಂಡರು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{apāyada suddi kēḷi janaru eccettukoṇḍaru.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Hearing the news of danger, people woke up to it.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \kn{ಎಚ್ಚೆತ್ತುಕೊಂಡೆ}, \emph{eccettukoṇḍe}.

Built with -\kn{ಕೊ}, for oneself.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಎಚ್ಚೆತ್ತುಕೊ}} (\emph{eccettuko}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 851 lists Kannada \emph{eccatt-}, \textquotedblleft{}to wake up\textquotedblright{}, here with -\emph{ko}, \textquotedblleft{}for oneself\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eccettuko}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eccettuko}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{apāyada suddi kēḷi janaru eccettukoṇḍaru.} — Hearing the news of danger, people woke up to it.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for unavoidable, then the Kannada for to waver, then say \emph{eccettuko} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಎಚ್ಚೆತ್ತುಕೊ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To wake up to\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಬಲವಂತ} (balavanta)}{ಬಲವಂತ (balavanta)}]{\kn{ಬಲವಂತ} (balavanta) — compulsion; force}

\label{lesson:KA-C420-balavanta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to waver, then the Kannada for to wake up to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಬಲವಂತ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಬಲವಂತ}} — \emph{balavanta} — \textquotedblleft{}compulsion; force\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಯಾರ} \kn{ಬಲವಂತವೂ} \kn{ಇಲ್ಲದೆ} \kn{ಅವನು} \kn{ಕೆಲಸ} \kn{ಬಿಟ್ಟನು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yāra balavantavū illade avanu kelasa biṭṭanu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He left the job without anyone forcing him.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಬಲವಂತವಾಗಿ}, by force; \kn{ಬಲವಂತ} \kn{ಮಾಡು}, to press someone.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಬಲವಂತ}} (\emph{balavanta}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{balavant}, \textquotedblleft{}strong\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9166), from \emph{bala}, \textquotedblleft{}strength\textquotedblright{}; Kannada uses it for force put on someone.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{balavanta}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{balavanta}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yāra balavantavū illade avanu kelasa biṭṭanu.} — He left the job without anyone forcing him.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to waver, then the Kannada for to wake up to, then say \emph{balavanta} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಬಲವಂತ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Compulsion; force\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ} (aniścita)}{ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ (aniścita)}]{\kn{ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ} (aniścita) — uncertain}

\label{lesson:KA-C420-aniscita}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to wake up to, then the Kannada for compulsion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ}} — \emph{aniścita} — \textquotedblleft{}uncertain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ನಾಳೆಯ} \kn{ಪಂದ್ಯ} \kn{ಇನ್ನೂ} \kn{ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nāḷeya pandya innū aniścita.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Tomorrow's match is still uncertain.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತತೆ}, uncertainty.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ}} (\emph{aniścita}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{aniścita}, \textquotedblleft{}unascertained, not certain\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aniścita}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aniścita}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nāḷeya pandya innū aniścita.} — Tomorrow's match is still uncertain.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to wake up to, then the Kannada for compulsion, then say \emph{aniścita} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Uncertain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಆಪತ್ತು} (āpattu)}{ಆಪತ್ತು (āpattu)}]{\kn{ಆಪತ್ತು} (āpattu) — a calamity; a mishap}

\label{lesson:KA-C420-apattu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for compulsion, then the Kannada for uncertain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಆಪತ್ತು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಆಪತ್ತು}} — \emph{āpattu} — \textquotedblleft{}a calamity; a mishap\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಆಪತ್ತಿನ} \kn{ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ನೆರೆಯವರು} \kn{ಸಹಾಯ} \kn{ಮಾಡಿದರು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āpattina samayadalli nereyavaru sahāya māḍidaru.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the time of trouble the neighbours helped.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಆಪತ್ತು} \kn{ಬರು}, for trouble to strike.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಆಪತ್ತು}} (\emph{āpattu}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{āpad}, \textquotedblleft{}misfortune, calamity\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1196), with the Kannada -\emph{u} after the final consonant.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āpattu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āpattu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āpattina samayadalli nereyavaru sahāya māḍidaru.} — In the time of trouble the neighbours helped.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for compulsion, then the Kannada for uncertain, then say \emph{āpattu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
